heading: Science-grade AI, built from Africa for industry and institutions
mission: We combine physics, data engineering and responsible AI to help industrial companies and public institutions turn data into reliable decisions that cut waste, downtime and risk, while training a new generation of African AI engineers.
vision: Trustworthy, science-grade AI for every factory and public institution, and proof that world-class AI engineering can be built from Africa.

approach.title: Physics first
approach.text: We start from the laws that govern your process: heat, mass, moisture, wear. Models built this way need less data and stay within physically possible values.

approach.title: Stated uncertainty
approach.text: Every forecast comes with a range and a plain account of its limits. We use the same methods as our founder's peer-reviewed work (JASA, 2026).

approach.title: Data foundations before models
approach.text: We test and reconcile data before we trust it.

approach.title: Humans in charge
approach.text: Every model has a named owner, and every automated action has an approval step.

approach.title: Documented by default

method.title: Discover

method.title: Build

method.title: Test

method.title: Hand over

title: Why every industrial forecast needs an error bar
excerpt: A single predicted number invites false confidence. A calibrated range tells operators when to act and when to check.

children.text: Most industrial AI tools give one number: the predicted moisture, the expected time to failure, the forecast energy use. That number looks precise, but it hides the question that matters on the shop floor: how far can I trust it today?

A forecast with a stated range answers that question. If the model predicts a bearing failure in 12 to 15 days, the maintenance team can plan. If the range is 2 to 40 days, the right action is to inspect, not to trust the model.

Conformal prediction is one practical way to produce such ranges. It wraps an existing model and uses held-out data to calibrate its intervals, so that a range labelled 90% contains the true value about 90% of the time. That guarantee rests on stated assumptions, which we check and document.
Physics helps too. A model that respects the laws governing the process (heat and moisture transfer, wear, flow) stays within physically possible values and needs less data to be useful.
Our rule is simple: no forecast leaves our hands without its range and the evidence behind it. That is what we mean by decisions you can verify.
